title: 49. Omega (June 2022)
name: QUESTIONS

You are the financial controller of Omega. a listed entity. One of Orrega’s directors has raised some queries

Currently unlisted and has two separate business segments which will complement the activities of our existing
group very well, | have been examining the most recent published financial statements of NewSub which are
prepared using full IFRS Accounting Standards. There are a few things that | do not understand about these
financial statements and | would appreciate your help.
The most recent published financial statements of NewSub are for the year ended 31 December 20X4. Given that
the Omega group year end is 31 March, this seems to pose a problem when preparing the consolidated financial
statements. How do we incorporate the NewSub results given that they are prepared to 2 different year-end date?
Could we require NewSub to change its year end, given we now control the company?
A key reason for my reviewing NewSub's published financial statements was to find out how revenues and profits
are split between its two business segments. | have found the searnental reports which we include in our
consolidated financial statements very useful when considering the performance of the business segments of our
existing group. However, when | examined the financial statements of NewSub, | found none of the segment
disclosures that | see when | review the consolidated financial statements of Omega. How can NewSub’s financial
statemants be in accordance with full IFRS Accounting Standards without this information? Does NewSub's lack of
segmental reporting mean we can ignore segmental reporting for NewSub in our consolidated financial staternents
| have noticed that NewSub has some investment properties. A note to NewSub’s financial statements states that
these properties are measured using the cost model. | believe that the Omega group policy is to measure
investment properties using the fair value model. This is in line with full IFRS Accounting Standards, so the NewSub
policy must be wrong. On that basis, how should we deal with the investment properties of NewSub in the
consolidated financial statements of Omega? Now that we control NewSub, should we require NewSub to change
its accounting policy in its own individual financial statements? (17 marks)
